bottleneck: Interoception — sensing the body's internal state — underlies emotion, anxiety, and disorders from depression to eating disorders, yet its neural pathways are far less mapped than vision or touch. How the insula and anterior cingulate construct feelings from visceral signals (heartbeat, gut, breath), and why the construction goes wrong in mental illness, lacks a mechanistic account. Interoceptive accuracy correlates with emotional awareness, but causal models and targeted interventions are missing — psychiatry cannot modulate a sense it has not mapped. The brain's sense of the body is its least understood sense, despite being the foundation of emotional life.
current_state: Interoceptive accuracy correlates with emotional awareness and is disrupted across psychiatric disorders, but causal models and targeted interventions are missing.

title: Interoception's neural basis barely mapped
why_it_blocks: Emotion, anxiety, and bodily self-awareness all run through interoception. Mapping it would ground psychiatry in physiology instead of symptom checklists — and open body-based interventions with mechanistic targets.
